beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — miRNA as volume knob
beats.narration_text: MicroRNAs are the genome's volume knobs. Each one clamps an mRNA strand and limits how much protein gets made. Several miRNAs target oncogene mRNAs — keeping growth signals quiet in normal cells. This plate shows what happens when the microRNA itself is lost.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — mRNA strand with miRNA clamp; protein output meter at low level; miRNA deleted — meter surges; caption: volume knob analogy for miRNA silencing

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — miR-15a/16 deletion in CLL, BCL-2 surge
beats.narration_text: Chromosome 13q14 deletions are common in CLL. They knock out miR-15a and miR-16, which normally suppress BCL-2 expression. Without the hairpin clamp, BCL-2 protein levels surge and cells become resistant to apoptosis. The deletion of a tiny non-coding RNA has exactly the same functional consequence as a BCL-2 amplification.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — stat card: 13q14 deletion in ~55% of CLL; miR-15a/16 → BCL-2 suppression; BCL-2 surge → apoptosis resistance; caption: one deleted hairpin, same as an amplification

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_MirDeletion class, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it. The mRNA strand is a Line at y equals plus one point five, x from minus five to plus three — BLUE, stroke six. The hairpin is an Arc above the midpoint — GREEN, open upward, radius zero point nine, angle PI. The block bar is a short horizontal Line below the arrow tip — GRAY. The separator is a DashedVMobject of a horizontal Line at y equals zero. The bottom state repeats the strand, replaces the hairpin with a VERM X-mark — two crossed Lines — removes the block bar, and clusters nine ORANGE dots below. All choreography is sequential — Create strand, FadeIn hairpin, grow arrow, then separator, then bottom state surge.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_MirDeletion
props.code:
# scenes.py — Claude Code output
BLUE="#0072B2"; GREEN="#009E73"
VERM="#D55E00"; ORANGE="#E69F00"; GRAY="#7c7c7c"

class B05_MirDeletion(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    # TOP STATE — silenced
    mrna_t=Line([-5.0,1.5,0],[3.0,1.5,0],
      color=BLUE,stroke_width=6)
    hairpin=Arc(radius=0.9,start_angle=0,
      angle=PI,color=GREEN,stroke_width=5
    ).move_to([0.0,1.5,0])
    arr_t=Arrow([2.5,1.5,0],[2.5,0.7,0],
      color=GRAY,stroke_width=3)
    block=Line([2.2,0.65,0],[2.8,0.65,0],
      color=GRAY,stroke_width=5)
    dot_t=Dot([2.5,0.45,0],radius=0.12,color=ORANGE)
    # SEPARATOR
    sep=DashedVMobject(
      Line([-5.5,0,0],[5.5,0,0],color=GRAY,stroke_width=1.5),
      num_dashes=22)
    # BOTTOM STATE — de-repressed
    mrna_b=Line([-5.0,-1.5,0],[3.0,-1.5,0],
      color=BLUE,stroke_width=6)
    xmark=VGroup(
      Line([-0.3,-1.2,0],[0.3,-1.8,0],color=VERM,stroke_width=6),
      Line([-0.3,-1.8,0],[0.3,-1.2,0],color=VERM,stroke_width=6))
    arr_b=Arrow([2.5,-1.5,0],[2.5,-2.3,0],
      color=GRAY,stroke_width=3)
    dots=VGroup(*[Dot(
      [2.5-0.4+(i%3)*0.4,-2.55+(i//3)*0.38,0],
      radius=0.12,color=ORANGE) for i in range(9)])
    self.play(Create(mrna_t),FadeIn(hairpin))
    self.play(GrowArrow(arr_t),FadeIn(block),FadeIn(dot_t))
    self.play(Create(sep))
    self.play(Create(mrna_b),FadeIn(xmark))
    self.play(GrowArrow(arr_b),
      LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(d) for d in dots],
      lag_ratio=0.08,run_time=1.0))
    self.wait(0.8)
props.sparkLine: Remove the clamp, nine times the output.

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_MirDeletion — top state then separator then bottom state
beats.narration_text: Run it. Top state: the BLUE mRNA strand creates, the GREEN hairpin arc appears above the midpoint — the silencer. The downward arrow grows, the block bar appears, and one ORANGE dot fades in — minimal output. The dashed separator draws across. Then the bottom state: another mRNA strand, the VERM X-mark where the hairpin was. The arrow grows unblocked, and nine ORANGE dots appear in rapid LaggedStart. One clamp removed. Nine times the output.

beats.act: OUTPUT — revised animation with surge transition
beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_MirDeletionSurge — hairpin FadeOut → X-mark Flash → dot surge → Wiggle
beats.narration_text: Watch the revision. The top state builds — mRNA strand, hairpin, blocked arrow, one dot. Then: the hairpin fades out. The X-mark appears with a Flash — the deletion event made visible. The block bar fades, the arrow grows unblocked. The dots surge from one to nine — rapid LaggedStart. And the cluster Wiggles. That Wiggle is not decoration. It is the protein surge that turns BCL-two into an apoptosis shield.

beats.role_note: What we built and what the motion taught
beats.narration_text: Remove the clamp, the mRNA runs free. The surge animation made the amplification physical — not a metaphor, just volume at full scale. One deleted hairpin, nine times the output.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — summary card: two-state before-after pattern; '1 hairpin deleted = 9× output'; 'clamp removal = amplification'; strip this for any repressor-removal mechanism

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: extend the mir-deletion animation — add a third panel showing what BCL-two overexpression downstream looks like — more pro-survival tokens on the apoptosis balance beam, beam tilting away from death. Connect the miRNA deletion to the apoptosis-momp plate's Stage 1. Why run it? Because connecting these two plates shows the full causal chain — the chromosome deletion causes the hairpin loss, the hairpin loss causes the BCL-two surge, and the BCL-two surge is exactly what tips the apoptosis balance beam. Gene deletion to apoptosis resistance — in geometry.
